flags.why: The adjective has a literary or formal register that the untagged gloss hides ([reference](https://tudientiengviet.org/uu-tu/)).
Using phụ tử for a father and son is literary rather than ordinary conversational Vietnamese ([dictionary](https://vdict.com/ph%E1%BB%A5%20t%E1%BB%AD%2C3%2C0%2C0.html)).
Cách ngôn belongs mainly to formal writing and speech, which the entry leaves unmarked ([dictionary](https://loigiaihay.com/tu-dien-tv/cach-ngon-eh6ZeYNsOhdoZ.html)).
The entry omits the common meaning 'disease; medical condition', encountered in expressions such as bệnh lý nền ([usage](https://www.vinmec.com/vie/bai-viet/nhung-benh-nao-goi-la-benh-nen-vi)).
flags.fix: Add a noun sense: disease; medical condition.

flags.why: The noun means the bits left after rendering fat, not any shrivelled chunk ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-t%C3%B3p)).
flags.fix: crackling; crispy bits left after rendering fat

flags.why: The entry omits the common meaning 'to shrivel or become shrunken', as in gầy tóp or tóp lại ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-t%C3%B3p)).
flags.fix: Add a sense: to shrivel; to become shrunken from drying out or losing weight.
